therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 80

results.target_engagement_evidence: HOMA-S increased 55.58% with Avandamet vs 18.65% with metformin (p<0.001); adiponectin increased 128.44% vs 12.96% (p<0.0001); fasting insulin decreased -35.2 pmol/L vs -1.5 pmol/L (p=0.0042)
biomarker_changes: Fasting insulin: -35.2 pmol/L (Avandamet) vs -1.5 pmol/L (metformin), difference -33.7 pmol/L (p=0.0042)
Lumbar spine BMD: +0.1% (Avandamet) vs -2.1% (metformin) at Week 80, difference -2.2% (p=0.0012)
Total hip BMD: -1.5% (Avandamet) vs 0.0% (metformin) at Week 80, difference -1.5% (p=0.0005)
Trochanter BMD: -2.1% (Avandamet) vs -0.1% (metformin) at Week 80, difference -1.9% (p=0.0038)
subgroup_findings: Female participants: lumbar spine BMD -2.7% (metformin) vs +0.2% (Avandamet) at Week 80 (difference -2.9%, p=0.0015)
Postmenopausal females: lumbar spine BMD -3.3% (metformin) vs 0% (Avandamet) at Week 80 (difference -3.3%, p=0.0161)
Premenopausal females: lumbar spine BMD -2.4% (metformin) vs -0.7% (Avandamet) at Week 80 (difference -1.7%, p=0.2363, NS)
Total hip BMD in females: -1.8% (Avandamet) vs 0.0% (metformin) at Week 80 (difference -1.7%, p=0.0152)
Trochanter BMD in females: -2.6% (Avandamet) vs -0.2% (metformin) at Week 80 (difference -2.4%, p=0.0330)
Treatment failure: 114 (Avandamet) vs 156 (metformin), HR=0.58 (95% CI: 0.45-0.74, p<0.0001)
FPG <=6.1 mmol/L at Week 80: 83 (Avandamet) vs 31 (metformin), OR=4.47 (p<0.0001)
safety_signals: Subcutaneous abscess higher in Avandamet arm (9/344 vs 1/334)
Avandamet associated with greater reduction in lumbar spine and hip BMD compared to metformin
Avandamet associated with increased total cholesterol and LDL vs metformin

dose_info.dose_modifications: Dose titration from level 1 (AVM 4mg/500mg or MET 500mg) up to level 4 (AVM 8mg/2000mg or MET 2000mg) based on glycemic response

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Rosiglitazone's PPAR-gamma agonism enhances insulin sensitization beyond metformin's AMPK-mediated hepatic glucose suppression, producing additive glycemic lowering and greater HOMA-S improvement in the combination arm
modulation_entries.citation: HOMA-S: percent difference from metformin = 31.14 (95% CI: 14.82–49.78), p = <0.001
